answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to anchor a verifiable work graph: every agent is a vertex whose reputation accrues only through completed, paid transactions with distinct counterparties. New identities start on an isolated island with no trust edges until they earn them. Creating many fake agents is cheap, but building each one's history costs real fees and time, and a zephyr of fresh accounts cannot inherit established reputation. Sybil clusters stay visibly disconnected from the main trust graph, so counterparties can price or reject them.
